why: All three checks pass. (1) VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md line 386 carries the quoted sentence exactly, as the third sentence of a three-sentence line tagged {/* min-version: 2.1.210 */}. The whole line does not reverse it: sentence 1 states Claude Code measures MEMORY.md against the 200-line and 25KB read limits after every write, sentence 2 documents the near-limit reminder ('keep one line per entry, move detail into topic files, and merge or drop stale entries'), sentence 3 is the quote. Line 388 (min-version 2.1.211) only refines WHAT is measured (frontmatter and block-level HTML comments stripped first). (2) CITED CODE: packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:90-91 is exactly `appendMemory(filePath, memory);` then `return successResponse(`Saved memory to ${filePath}`);` — unconditional, no measurement, no branch. appendMemory (:39-49) reads, formats, atomically renames and returns void; the only pre-write guards in handleRemember are memoryEnabled, empty-string, and unresolvable-scope. successResponse (response.ts:13-19) adds nothing. (3) LAYER UP/DOWN: the sibling writer appendMemoryFile (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:122-132) is byte-for-byte the same shape and also measures nothing; the tool description the model reads before calling (tool-defs.ts:584) carries no conciseness, index, topic-file or limit guidance; grep -ran over packages/ and apps/ for a 25KB constant, 'read limit', 'memory index', 'rewrite the index' or 'shorten' finds nothing in the memory subsystem. Two adjacent mechanisms exist and neither is this one, so name them before rebuilding: (a) runScheduledAutoMemoryCleanup (memory-cleanup.ts:260) is a DAILY, deterministic pass that drops only marker-tagged duplicate and >30-day entries, never bounds the file to 200 lines or 25KB, and skips any file over AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES=256KB — the opposite trigger and the opposite audience from a synchronous post-write error to the model; (b) the `trim_memory_files` suggestion (packages/pi-agent-server/src/context-categories.ts:239-247) is a human-facing /context overlay hint fired on token SHARE via isWorthAdvising, not on MEMORY.md's read limit, and never reaches the model. Subsystem is correctly named: this is the auto-memory index, not a sibling. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (none of the nine touches memory). NOT a de-brand or dropped-subscription product difference. The nearest recorded decision is the parity audit's 'ahead' row (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:757 — 'Claude: Reactive post-write reminders only · ours: Scheduled marker-scoped cleanup'), but it does not cover this: the audit's own re-verification at :1669 (item 12) records that that row's characterisation of Claude's side was STALE and that the documented load limit is part of the subsystem. Being ahead on scheduled cleanup does not supply the synchronous over-limit error.
correctedState: Confirmed as stated, with two sharpenings an executor needs. (a) The absence is the whole write path, not just the tool's return: handleRemember (remember.ts:90-91) and its writer appendMemory (:39-49), plus the sibling appendMemoryFile (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:122-132), perform no post-write measurement; there is no 25KB byte constant anywhere in the memory subsystem (only MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200 at memory-store.ts:8), no near-limit reminder, and no frontmatter/HTML-comment exclusion. (b) The doc's stated RATIONALE ('everything past the limit is dropped on the next load') holds only on our legacy fallback composer: loadMemoryPromptBlock → readMemoryFile (memory-store.ts:29-32) does slice to 200 lines and drop the rest silently, but the LIVE capability path reads MEMORY.md in full through materializer.readText (capabilities/materializer.ts:179-186) and pins it verbatim (base-agent.ts:~996-1006), so on the shipped path nothing is dropped — the file simply grows unbounded in the pinned block (the separate f098/f104 gap). So the missing behaviour is real on both paths, but the harm differs by path: silent truncation on the legacy path, unbounded context cost on the live one. Also note our fork has no memory DIRECTORY with topic files (session = <dataPath>/MEMORY.md, project = <cwd>/MEMORY.md, user = <configDir>/MEMORY.md), so the remedy Claude's error instructs ('move detail into topic files, rewrite the index') has no target here — any port must decide what the error should tell the model to do.
